commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning

Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

## 전체 흐름

```
복합 명령의 종료 코드 = "마지막" 명령의 종료 코드

errexit (set -e) = "비0 = 즉시 종료" (조건문·&&/|| 앞쪽 등 예외 제외)
  종료 코드가 계약인 프로그램(훅: 0=통과, 2=차단)

```

## 핵심 문장

- 파이프라인·그룹·순차 명령의 종료 코드는 **마지막 명령**의 것이다 — 앞 단계 실패는 명시적으로 캡처하지 않으면 사라진다.

10	`${PIPESTATUS[0]}`는 파이프라인 각 명령의 rc 배열이라 원 명령의 rc를 직접 꺼낼 수 있다.\
11	기록된 해결은 원 명령의 출력을 로그 파일로 받고 rc를 마커로 남기는 것이었다: `(cmd > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> log)`.
12	   > **pipefail** — 파이프라인 중 하나라도 실패하면 파이프라인 전체를 실패로 보게 하는 bash 옵션.
13	
14	2. **순차 명령의 rc = 마지막 명령.** `-e` 없이 이어 쓴 스크립트의 종료 코드는 마지막 명령의 것이다.\
15	중간 단계가 매번 traceback으로 죽어도 마지막 명령이 성공하면 스크립트는 0으로 끝나고, 스케줄러는 SUCCESS를 기록한다.\
16	단계마다 rc를 캡처해 누적하고 마지막에 `exit "$rc"`로 내보낸다.\
17	실패 알림 경로(스케줄러의 실패 훅)도 없어서 발견이 늦었다 — rc가 정직해도 그것을 듣는 쪽이 있어야 한다.

# issue/shell/exit-status-semantics — 정답

태그: `silent-failure`

## 정답
<!-- 질문 1:1 대응 -->

1. **파이프라인의 rc = 마지막 명령.** `$?`는 `tail`의 종료 코드 0이다 — 빌드 도구의 실패는 사라진다.\
`set -o pipefail`을 켜면 파이프라인의 rc가 "비0으로 끝난 가장 오른쪽 명령"의 것이 되어 앞 단계 실패가 드러난다.\
`${PIPESTATUS[0]}`는 파이프라인 각 명령의 rc 배열이라 원 명령의 rc를 직접 꺼낼 수 있다.\
기록된 해결은 원 명령의 출력을 로그 파일로 받고 rc를 마커로 남기는 것이었다: `(cmd > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> log)`.
   > **pipefail** — 파이프라인 중 하나라도 실패하면 파이프라인 전체를 실패로 보게 하는 bash 옵션.

2. **순차 명령의 rc = 마지막 명령.** `-e` 없이 이어 쓴 스크립트의 종료 코드는 마지막 명령의 것이다.\
중간 단계가 매번 traceback으로 죽어도 마지막 명령이 성공하면 스크립트는 0으로 끝나고, 스케줄러는 SUCCESS를 기록한다.\
단계마다 rc를 캡처해 누적하고 마지막에 `exit "$rc"`로 내보낸다.\
실패 알림 경로(스케줄러의 실패 훅)도 없어서 발견이 늦었다 — rc가 정직해도 그것을 듣는 쪽이 있어야 한다.

3. **그룹 리다이렉트는 앞 단계 실패를 삼킨다.** `{ cat; printf; }`의 rc는 `printf`의 것이다.\
`cat`이 읽기에 실패해도 `printf`가 성공하면 그룹은 0 → `&& mv`가 실행되어 **새 줄 하나만 든 TMP가 원본을 덮어쓴다**.\
단계마다 rc를 검사해 실패하면 TMP를 지우고 빠져나가야 한다.\
같은 부류: `{ ... } >> "$LOG"`에서 리다이렉트 대상에 쓸 수 없으면 블록이 실행되지 않는다 — 그 그룹의 rc는 1(bash)이지만 아무도 검사하지 않아 스크립트는 뒤 명령의 rc로 성공처럼 끝났다 — 로그 쓰기 가능 여부를 먼저 검사하고 전용 rc로 끝낸다.

4. **errexit와 종료 코드 계약.** `set -e`는 예상 못 한 하위 명령 실패를 "그 명령의 rc로 즉시 종료"로 바꾼다.\
`jq`가 손상 JSON에 exit 2를 내면 스크립트도 exit 2로 끝나는데, 호출자 계약에서 2는 "차단"이다 — 파싱 오류가 사용자 프롬프트 차단으로 둔갑한다(사건 환경 기준 — 입력 파싱 오류의 jq 종료 코드는 버전마다 다르다(예: jq 1.7은 5). 어느 값이든 계약 밖 코드이거나 우연히 계약 코드와 겹친다는 점이 문제다).\
`$(( 09 ))`는 선행 0 때문에 8진수로 해석되어 오류가 난다 — 이것은 `set -e`와 무관하게 비대화형 bash를 즉시 종료시키는 확장 오류라(rc 1) 역시 계약 밖 조기 종료다.\
교정: jq 대입은 실패 시 빈 값을 주는 헬퍼로, 산술은 `10#$n`으로 10진 강제, `jq -e .`는 비객체 JSON(`5`)도 통과시키므로 `type=="object"`로 검사, 명령 치환은 `|| VAR=""` 가드.\
모든 실패가 exit 0으로 수렴해야 하는 관측 전용 스크립트는 아예 `set -e`를 쓰지 않았다.
   > **errexit(set -e)** — 명령이 비0을 반환하면 셸을 즉시 종료시키는 옵션. `if`/`while` 조건, `&&`·`||` 목록의 마지막이 아닌 명령, `!` 부정, (pipefail 없을 때) 파이프라인의 마지막이 아닌 명령은 예외.

5. **비0 ≠ 실패.** `grep`의 1은 "매칭 없음"이라는 정상 결과이고, `iconv`는 불완전 꼬리를 만나면 유효한 접두를 이미 출력한 뒤 비0을 낸다.\
`grep ... && 다음단계`는 매칭 0건에서 다음 단계를 조용히 건너뛴다.\
`out=$(iconv ...) || out="$raw"`처럼 비0을 "읽기 실패 폴백"으로 쓰자, 정상적인 부분 변환이 매번 폴백으로 빠져 원시 절단(문자 중간이 잘린 바이트열)으로 회귀했다.\
교정은 `out=$(iconv ... || true)` — rc는 무시하고 **출력을 채택**, 출력이 없을 때만 폴백.

6. **자르기와 가리기.** 둘 다 "오류 신호 없이 정보가 사라진다"가 공통이다.\
`head -400`은 초과분을 rc 0으로 버려서, 잘린 입력을 받은 소비자(리뷰어)가 판정할 근거를 잃었다 — 소비자는 입력이 잘렸다는 사실을 모른다.\
반증: 자른 경우 절단 구간을 직접 다시 확인하고, 종료 코드는 원 명령의 rc 마커로 판정한다.

7. **rc 너머를 본다.** 종료 코드 0은 "마지막 명령이 0을 냈다"일 뿐이다.\
빌드·테스트는 리포트 파일(BUILD 결과·테스트 수)을 직접 읽고, 배치는 단계별 rc와 산출물을 확인하고, 스텁으로 각 실패 경로를 일부러 재현해 **기대한 종료 코드가 나오는지** 음성 검증한다.\
테스트 수가 워커마다 다르게 보고되면 메인이 직접 재실행해 정합을 확인한다.

## 문제 구조 (추상화 코드)

### 변형 A — 파이프라인이 원 명령의 실패를 가림
① 문제 코드
```sh
build-tool test 2>&1 | tail -25          # rc = tail = 0
echo "exit=$?"                           # 0 → "green" 보고
build-tool verify | grep -E 'Tests|BUILD' | tail -5
```
② 고친 코드
```sh
( build-tool verify > build.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> build.log )
grep -q '^EXIT=0$' build.log || fail "build failed"
# 또는
build-tool test | tail -25; rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
# 또는 스크립트 상단
set -o pipefail
```
무엇이 깨졌나: 파이프라인의 rc가 마지막 명령(tail)의 것이었다.\
같은 구조: 빌드 실패를 모른 채 다음 단계(기존 서비스 정지)로 진행 → 교체는 빌드 성공 확인 뒤에만.

### 변형 B — `-e` 없는 순차 스크립트
① 문제 코드
```sh
echo "--- step A ---"; run step_a
echo "--- step B ---"; run step_b          # 스크립트 rc = 마지막 명령
```
② 고친 코드
```sh
rc=0
run step_a; a_rc=$?
if [ "$a_rc" -ne 0 ]; then echo "!!! step_a failed (exit=$a_rc)"; rc=$a_rc; fi
run step_b; b_rc=$?
if [ "$b_rc" -ne 0 ]; then echo "!!! step_b failed (exit=$b_rc)"; rc=$b_rc; fi
exit "$rc"
```
무엇이 깨졌나: 중간 단계 실패가 스크립트 종료 코드에 반영되지 않았다.

### 변형 C — 그룹 리다이렉트
① 문제 코드
```sh
{ cat "$SRC"; printf '%s\n' "$LINE"; } > "$TMP" && mv "$TMP" "$SRC"   # cat 실패 → 원본 덮어씀
{ main_body; } >> "$LOG"                                             # LOG 쓰기 불가 → 본문 미실행 (그룹 rc 1, 미검사 → 스크립트는 성공처럼 종료)
```
② 고친 코드
```sh
cat "$SRC" > "$TMP"            || { rm -f "$TMP"; exit 0; }   # 사건은 관측 전용 훅이라 0으로 수렴 — 일반 스크립트면 비0으로 끝낸다
printf '%s\n' "$LINE" >> "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; exit 0; }
mv -f "$TMP" "$SRC"            || rm -f "$TMP"

[ -w "$LOG_DIR" ] || exit 90                                         # 로그 쓰기 사전검사 (전용 rc)
```
무엇이 깨졌나: 복합 명령의 rc가 마지막 단계의 것이라 앞 단계 실패가 가려졌다.

### 변형 D — 종료 코드가 계약인 스크립트의 errexit
① 문제 코드
```sh
set -eu
field=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.field')      # 손상 JSON → jq 비0(사건 버전 2) → 스크립트 exit 2 (= 차단)
n=$(( ts ))                                         # ts=09 → 8진수 오류 → 조기 종료 (set -e 무관, rc 1)
printf '%s' "$input" | jq -e . >/dev/null           # 5 같은 비객체도 통과 → 이후 필드 접근에서 사망
```
② 고친 코드
```sh
set -eu
jqr() { printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; }   # 실패 = 빈 값(무해)
field=$(jqr '.field')
n=$(( 10#$ts ))
printf '%s' "$input" | jq -e 'type=="object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "warn: bad input" >&2; exit 0; }
val=$(some_subst) || val=""
```
무엇이 깨졌나: "모든 실패 = 즉시 종료"가 호출자와의 종료 코드 계약(0/2)을 깨뜨렸다.\
같은 구조: 빈 stdin이 경고 없이 통과, 날짜 파싱 실패로 조기 종료 → 경고 1줄·승인 무효로 처리.

### 변형 E — 명령별 비0 의미를 실패로 오해
① 문제 코드
```sh
grep -q "$pat" "$f" && invoke_next_step            # 0건 = rc 1 → 후속 단계 미발화
out=$(iconv -f A -t B -c <<<"$raw") || out="$raw"   # 불완전 꼬리 rc≠0 → 정상 경로가 폴백으로
head -400 packet > review_input                    # 초과분 무음 절단
```
② 고친 코드
```sh

# settle — 파트너 일일 정산 배치

파트너 ERP가 매일 밤 떨궈 주는 고정폭 피드(`feed-YYYYMMDD.dat`)와 거래처 마스터(`partners.dat`)를 읽어,
정산 데스크용 텍스트 리포트와 회계 시스템용 CSV를 만든다.

## 실행

```
bin/settle run 20261005        # stage → normalize → aggregate → publish
bin/settle report 20261005     # 게시된 리포트 출력
bin/settle export 20261005     # 게시된 CSV 출력
bin/settle partner P10003      # 마스터 항목 조회
bin/settle check 20261005      # 트레일러 대조(건수·합계) 재검사
```

스케줄러(cron)는 매일 06:10에 `bin/settle run $(date -d yesterday +%Y%m%d)` 를 돌리고, exit 0이 아니면 당직에게 알린다.

## 구성

| 경로 | 내용 |
|------|------|
| `bin/settle` | 진입점. 서브커맨드 분기, 단계 순차 실행 |
| `steps/NN-*.sh` | 단계 스크립트(번호 순 실행). 각자 `_env.sh`로 lib·설정을 읽는다 |
| `lib/` | 공용 함수 (피드 해석, 마스터, 캐시, 금액, 리포트, CSV 등) |
| `conf/settle.conf` | 디렉토리·인코딩·리포트 설정. `SETTLE_*` 환경변수로 덮어쓴다 |
| `conf/layout.conf` | 피드 레코드 바이트 레이아웃(ERP-IF-07 rev.3) |
| `fixtures/` | 샘플 피드·마스터 (운영 데이터에서 금액·이름을 바꾼 것) |
| `tests/` | `bash tests/run.sh` — 단위 테스트 + 샘플 일자 E2E |

## 산출물

- `$OUT_DIR/report-YYYYMMDD.txt` — 거래처별 건수·금액, 비활성 거래처 제외
- `$OUT_DIR/export-YYYYMMDD.csv` — 레코드 단위, UTF-8, 헤더 `date,seq,code,partner,amount,memo`
- `$WORK_DIR/YYYYMMDD/` — 단계 중간 산출물(`feed.dat`, `normalized.tsv`, `totals.tsv`)

## 피드 규격 메모

- 레코드 64바이트 고정, H(헤더) / D(명세) / T(트레일러).
- 금액은 12자리 0 채움 원 단위. 구버전 ERP는 환불을 끝자리 `-`로 표시한다.
- 거래처명 20바이트, 적요 12바이트, 남는 자리는 공백으로 채운다.
- 트레일러의 건수·합계가 읽은 값과 다르면 normalize 단계에서 중단한다.

=== bin/settle
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# settle — partner settlement batch.
#
#   settle run DATE        stage → normalize → aggregate → publish
#   settle report DATE     print the published report
#   settle export DATE     print the published CSV export
#   settle partner CODE    show the master entry for CODE
#   settle check DATE      re-verify control totals of a staged feed
#
# DATE is YYYYMMDD. Configuration: conf/settle.conf (SETTLE_* overrides).
set -u
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
SETTLE_HOME=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
export SETTLE_HOME
. "$SETTLE_HOME/steps/_env.sh"

usage() { sed -n '3,10p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

cmd_run() {
  local date=$1 step rc
  for step in "$SETTLE_HOME"/steps/[0-9][0-9]-*.sh; do
    bash "$step" "$date"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
      warn "step $(basename "$step") failed (exit $rc)"
      return "$rc"
    fi
  done
  log "run $date complete"
}

cmd_show() {
  local f="$OUT_DIR/$1-$2.$3"
  require_file "$f" "$1"
  cat "$f"
}

cmd_partner() {
  local code=$1
  partners_load 2>/dev/null
  if ! cache_get partners "$code" >/dev/null; then
    echo "no such partner: $code" >&2
    return 4
  fi
  printf 'code:   %s\nname:   %s\nstatus: %s\n' "$code" "$(partner_name "$code")" \
    "$(cache_get partner_status "$code")"
}

cmd_check() {
  local dir
  dir=$(run_dir "$(check_date "$1")")
  require_file "$dir/normalized.tsv" "normalized records"
  ledger_check "$dir/feed.dat" "$dir/normalized.tsv" && echo "control totals OK"
}

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { usage; exit 64; }
cmd=$1; shift
case "$cmd" in
  run)     [ $# -eq 1 ] || { usage; exit 64; }; cmd_run "$(check_date "$1")" ;;

# cache.sh — tiny key/value cache kept under the run's work directory so
# that repeated lookups (partner names, mostly) do not re-read the master.
#
# File format: one "key<TAB>value" per line, file per namespace.

cache_file() { printf '%s/cache/%s.kv' "$WORK_DIR" "$1"; }

cache_init() {
  ensure_dir "$WORK_DIR/cache"
  : > "$(cache_file "$1")"
}

# cache_put NS KEY VALUE — replaces any previous value for KEY.
cache_put() {
  local f tmp
  f=$(cache_file "$1")
  tmp="$f.$$"
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    awk -F '\t' -v k="$2" '$1 != k' "$f" > "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
  else
    : > "$tmp"
  fi
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$2" "$3" >> "$tmp"
  mv -f "$tmp" "$f"
}

# cache_get NS KEY — prints the value; fails when KEY is absent.
cache_get() {
  local f
  f=$(cache_file "$1")
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 1
  LC_ALL=C awk -F '\t' -v k="$2" '
    $1 == k { printf "%s", substr($0, length(k) + 2); found = 1; exit }
    END { exit !found }
  ' "$f"
}

# cache_stamp NS SOURCE — remembers SOURCE's mtime; cache_fresh compares.
cache_stamp() { stat -c %Y "$2" > "$(cache_file "$1").stamp" 2>/dev/null; }

cache_fresh() {
  local s
  s=$(cat "$(cache_file "$1").stamp" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [ "$s" = "$(stat -c %Y "$2" 2>/dev/null)" ]
}

# charset.sh — conversion between the partner ERP code page and UTF-8.
# Everything this tool writes (reports, exports, lookups) is UTF-8.

# charset_to_utf8 TEXT [ENCODING]
#   Converts TEXT from ENCODING (default FEED_ENCODING) to UTF-8.
charset_to_utf8() {
  local raw=$1 enc=${2:-$FEED_ENCODING} out
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  case "$enc" in
    UTF-8|utf-8|UTF8|utf8) printf '%s' "$raw"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  out=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | iconv -f "$enc" -t UTF-8 -c 2>/dev/null) || out=$raw
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

# charset_is_utf8 TEXT — succeeds when TEXT is well-formed UTF-8.
charset_is_utf8() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# charset_check_file FILE — succeeds when the whole file is well-formed UTF-8.
charset_check_file() {
  iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# Removes carriage returns left by the ERP's Windows transfer job.
charset_strip_cr() {
  local s=$1
  printf '%s' "${s//$'\r'/}"
}

# feed.sh — reader for the partner ERP fixed-width feed (see conf/layout.conf).
#
# feed_records FILE
#   Prints one TAB-separated line per detail record, already in UTF-8:
#     date  seq  code  name  amount  memo
#   Header/trailer records are skipped; use feed_trailer for the trailer.

# layout_slice LINE OFFSET:LENGTH — byte slice (caller runs under LC_ALL=C).
layout_slice() {
  local spec=$2
  printf '%s' "${1:${spec%%:*}:${spec##*:}}"
}

feed_records() (
  export LC_ALL=C
  local file=$1 line type n=0 seq code name amount memo date
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    line=$(charset_strip_cr "$line")
    type=$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_TYPE")
    [ "$type" = D ] || continue
    if [ "${#line}" -ne 64 ]; then
      warn "line $n: record length ${#line}, expected 64 — skipped"
      continue
    fi
    date=$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_DATE")
    seq=$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_SEQ")
    code=$(text_trim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_CODE")")
    name=$(text_rtrim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_NAME")")
    amount=$(money_parse "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_AMOUNT")") || {
      warn "line $n: bad amount — skipped"; continue; }
    memo=$(text_rtrim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_MEMO")")
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$date" "$((10#$seq))" "$code" \
      "$(charset_to_utf8 "$name")" "$amount" "$(charset_to_utf8 "$memo")"
  done < "$file"
)

# feed_header FILE — prints "date<TAB>source" from the H record.
feed_header() (
  export LC_ALL=C
  local line
  IFS= read -r line < "$1" || exit 1
  line=$(charset_strip_cr "$line")
  [ "$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_TYPE")" = H ] || exit 1
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_DATE")" \
    "$(text_rtrim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$H_SOURCE")")"
)

# feed_trailer FILE — prints "count<TAB>total" from the T record.
feed_trailer() (
  export LC_ALL=C
  local line last=""
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    line=$(charset_strip_cr "$line")
    [ "$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_TYPE")" = T ] && last=$line
  done < "$1"
  [ -n "$last" ] || exit 1
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$((10#$(layout_slice "$last" "$T_COUNT")))" \
    "$((10#$(layout_slice "$last" "$T_TOTAL")))"
)

# ledger.sh — aggregation and control totals.

# ledger_totals NORMALIZED_TSV — per partner "code<TAB>count<TAB>sum<TAB>feedname",
# sorted by code. The feed name of the first record is kept for partners
# missing from the master.
ledger_totals() {
  awk -F '\t' '
    { c[$3]++; s[$3] += $5; if (!($3 in nm)) nm[$3] = $4 }
    END { for (k in c) printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\n", k, c[k], s[k], nm[k] }
  ' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k1,1
}

# ledger_sum NORMALIZED_TSV — "count<TAB>total" over all records.
ledger_sum() {
  awk -F '\t' '{ n++; t += $5 } END { printf "%d\t%d\n", n, t }' "$1"
}

# ledger_check FEED NORMALIZED_TSV — compares the trailer with what we read.
ledger_check() {
  local want got
  want=$(feed_trailer "$1") || { warn "no trailer in $1"; return 2; }
  got=$(ledger_sum "$2")
  if [ "$want" != "$got" ]; then
    warn "control totals differ: trailer=${want//$'\t'/ / } read=${got//$'\t'/ / }"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# money.sh — amounts in the feed are zero-padded whole won, 12 digits,
# with a trailing "-" in place of the last pad digit for refunds
# (e.g. "00000035000-" is -35000 on the older ERP build).

money_parse() {
  local s=$1 neg=0
  s=${s// /}
  if [ "${s: -1}" = "-" ]; then neg=1; s=${s%-}; fi
  case "$s" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  s=$((10#$s))
  if [ "$neg" -eq 1 ]; then s=$(( -s )); fi
  printf '%d' "$s"
}

# money_fmt 1250000 -> 1,250,000
money_fmt() {
  local n=$1 sign="" out=""
  if [ "${n:0:1}" = "-" ]; then sign="-"; n=${n#-}; fi
  while [ ${#n} -gt 3 ]; do
    out=",${n: -3}$out"
    n=${n:0:${#n}-3}
  done
  printf '%s%s%s' "$sign" "$n" "$out"
}

# partners.sh — partner master lookups.
#
# The master is exported by the same ERP as the feed, pipe-delimited:
#   CODE|NAME|REGION|STATUS        (STATUS: A active, I inactive)
# Names are loaded once per run into the "partners" cache.

partners_load() {
  local code name region status n=0
  require_file "$MASTER_FILE" "partner master"
  if cache_fresh partners "$MASTER_FILE" && [ -s "$(cache_file partners)" ]; then
    return 0
  fi
  cache_init partners
  cache_init partner_status
  while IFS='|' read -r code name region status || [ -n "$code" ]; do
    code=$(text_trim "$code")
    case "$code" in ''|\#*) continue ;; esac
    name=$(charset_strip_cr "$name")
    status=$(charset_strip_cr "$status")
    cache_put partners "$code" "$(charset_to_utf8 "$name")"
    cache_put partner_status "$code" "${status:-A}"
    n=$((n + 1))
  done < "$MASTER_FILE"
  cache_stamp partners "$MASTER_FILE"
  log "partner master: $n entries"
}

# partner_name CODE [DEFAULT] — display name for CODE.
partner_name() {
  local v
  if v=$(cache_get partners "$1") && [ -n "$v" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$v"
  elif [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$2"
  else
    printf '(unknown %s)' "$1"
  fi
}

partner_active() {
  local s
  s=$(cache_get partner_status "$1") || return 0
  [ "$s" != I ]
}

# report_render DATE TOTALS_TSV FEED_SOURCE
report_render() {
  local date=$1 totals=$2 source=$3 code cnt sum feedname name
  local all_cnt=0 all_sum=0 skipped=0 w=$REPORT_NAME_WIDTH
  printf '%s  %s  (source: %s)\n' "$REPORT_TITLE" "$(date_dash "$date")" "$source"
  printf '%s\n' "$(printf '%*s' $(( 8 + w + 22 )) '' | tr ' ' '=')"

  while IFS=$'\t' read -r code cnt sum feedname; do
    [ -n "$code" ] || continue
    if [ "${REPORT_SKIP_INACTIVE:-0}" = 1 ] && ! partner_active "$code"; then
      skipped=$((skipped + 1))
      continue
    fi
    name=$(partner_name "$code" "$feedname")
    printf '%-8s%s%6d%16s\n' "$code" "$(text_pad "$name" "$w")" "$cnt" "$(money_fmt "$sum")"

    all_sum=$((all_sum + sum))

  printf '%-8s%s%6d%16s\n' "" "$(text_pad "합계" "$w")" "$all_cnt" "$(money_fmt "$all_sum")"
  if [ "$skipped" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '(inactive partners omitted: %d)\n' "$skipped"
  fi
}

# text.sh — trimming and column layout for the text report.
# Hangul and other non-ASCII characters take two terminal columns.

text_rtrim() {
  local s=$1
  printf '%s' "${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
}

text_ltrim() {
  local s=$1
  printf '%s' "${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
}

text_trim() { text_ltrim "$(text_rtrim "$1")"; }

# Number of terminal columns TEXT occupies.
text_width() {
  local s=$1 ascii
  ascii=${s//[^[:ascii:]]/}
  printf '%d' $(( ${#ascii} + 2 * (${#s} - ${#ascii}) ))
}

# text_fit TEXT COLS — cut TEXT so that it fits in COLS columns, marking
# the cut with "~".
text_fit() {
  local s=$1 cols=$2 out="" ch w=0 cw i
  if [ "$(text_width "$s")" -le "$cols" ]; then printf '%s' "$s"; return; fi
  for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
    ch=${s:i:1}
    if [[ $ch == [[:ascii:]] ]]; then cw=1; else cw=2; fi
    (( w + cw > cols - 1 )) && break
    out+=$ch; w=$(( w + cw ))
  done
  printf '%s~' "$out"
}

# text_pad TEXT COLS — left-aligned, padded with spaces to COLS columns.
text_pad() {
  local s w
  s=$(text_fit "$1" "$2")
  w=$(text_width "$s")
  printf '%s%*s' "$s" $(( $2 - w )) ''
}

# text_lpad TEXT COLS — right-aligned.
text_lpad() {
  local w
  w=$(text_width "$1")
  printf '%*s%s' $(( $2 > w ? $2 - w : 0 )) '' "$1"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# settle — partner settlement batch.
#
#   settle run DATE        stage → normalize → aggregate → publish
#   settle report DATE     print the published report
#   settle export DATE     print the published CSV export
#   settle partner CODE    show the master entry for CODE
#   settle check DATE      re-verify control totals of a staged feed
#
# DATE is YYYYMMDD. Configuration: conf/settle.conf (SETTLE_* overrides).
set -u
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
SETTLE_HOME=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
export SETTLE_HOME
. "$SETTLE_HOME/steps/_env.sh"

usage() { sed -n '3,10p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

cmd_run() {
  local date=$1 step rc
  for step in "$SETTLE_HOME"/steps/[0-9][0-9]-*.sh; do
    bash "$step" "$date"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
      warn "step $(basename "$step") failed (exit $rc)"
      return "$rc"
    fi
  done
  log "run $date complete"
}

cmd_show() {
  local f="$OUT_DIR/$1-$2.$3"
  require_file "$f" "$1"
  cat "$f"
}

cmd_partner() {
  local code=$1
  partners_load 2>/dev/null
  if ! cache_get partners "$code" >/dev/null; then
    echo "no such partner: $code" >&2
    return 4
  fi
  printf 'code:   %s\nname:   %s\nstatus: %s\n' "$code" "$(partner_name "$code")" \
    "$(cache_get partner_status "$code")"
}

cmd_check() {
  local dir
  dir=$(run_dir "$(check_date "$1")")
  require_file "$dir/normalized.tsv" "normalized records"
  ledger_check "$dir/feed.dat" "$dir/normalized.tsv" && echo "control totals OK"
}

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { usage; exit 64; }
cmd=$1; shift
case "$cmd" in
  run)     [ $# -eq 1 ] || { usage; exit 64; }; cmd_run "$(check_date "$1")" ;;
  report)  [ $# -eq 1 ] || { usage; exit 64; }; cmd_show report "$(check_date "$1")" txt ;;
  export)  [ $# -eq 1 ] || { usage; exit 64; }; cmd_show export "$(check_date "$1")" csv ;;

# cache.sh — tiny key/value cache kept under the run's work directory so
# that repeated lookups (partner names, mostly) do not re-read the master.
#
# File format: one "key<TAB>value" per line, file per namespace.

cache_file() { printf '%s/cache/%s.kv' "$WORK_DIR" "$1"; }

cache_init() {
  ensure_dir "$WORK_DIR/cache"
  : > "$(cache_file "$1")"
}

# cache_put NS KEY VALUE — replaces any previous value for KEY.
cache_put() {
  local f tmp
  f=$(cache_file "$1")
  tmp="$f.$$"
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    awk -F '\t' -v k="$2" '$1 != k' "$f" > "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
  else
    : > "$tmp"
  fi
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$2" "$3" >> "$tmp"
  mv -f "$tmp" "$f"
}

# cache_get NS KEY — prints the value; fails when KEY is absent.
cache_get() {
  local f
  f=$(cache_file "$1")
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 1
  LC_ALL=C awk -F '\t' -v k="$2" '
    $1 == k { printf "%s", substr($0, length(k) + 2); found = 1; exit }
    END { exit !found }
  ' "$f"
}

# cache_stamp NS SOURCE — remembers SOURCE's mtime; cache_fresh compares.
cache_stamp() { stat -c %Y "$2" > "$(cache_file "$1").stamp" 2>/dev/null; }

cache_fresh() {
  local s
  s=$(cat "$(cache_file "$1").stamp" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [ "$s" = "$(stat -c %Y "$2" 2>/dev/null)" ]
}

# charset.sh — conversion between the partner ERP code page and UTF-8.
# Everything this tool writes (reports, exports, lookups) is UTF-8.

# charset_to_utf8 TEXT [ENCODING]
#   Converts TEXT from ENCODING (default FEED_ENCODING) to UTF-8.
charset_to_utf8() {
  local raw=$1 enc=${2:-$FEED_ENCODING} out
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  case "$enc" in
    UTF-8|utf-8|UTF8|utf8) printf '%s' "$raw"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  out=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | iconv -f "$enc" -t UTF-8 -c 2>/dev/null) || out=$raw
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

# charset_is_utf8 TEXT — succeeds when TEXT is well-formed UTF-8.
charset_is_utf8() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# charset_check_file FILE — succeeds when the whole file is well-formed UTF-8.
charset_check_file() {
  iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# Removes carriage returns left by the ERP's Windows transfer job.
charset_strip_cr() {
  local s=$1
  printf '%s' "${s//$'\r'/}"
}

# feed.sh — reader for the partner ERP fixed-width feed (see conf/layout.conf).
#
# feed_records FILE
#   Prints one TAB-separated line per detail record, already in UTF-8:
#     date  seq  code  name  amount  memo
#   Header/trailer records are skipped; use feed_trailer for the trailer.

# layout_slice LINE OFFSET:LENGTH — byte slice (caller runs under LC_ALL=C).
layout_slice() {
  local spec=$2
  printf '%s' "${1:${spec%%:*}:${spec##*:}}"
}

feed_records() (
  export LC_ALL=C
  local file=$1 line type n=0 seq code name amount memo date
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    line=$(charset_strip_cr "$line")
    type=$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_TYPE")
    [ "$type" = D ] || continue
    if [ "${#line}" -ne 64 ]; then
      warn "line $n: record length ${#line}, expected 64 — skipped"
      continue
    fi
    date=$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_DATE")
    seq=$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_SEQ")
    code=$(text_trim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_CODE")")
    name=$(text_rtrim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_NAME")")
    amount=$(money_parse "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_AMOUNT")") || {
      warn "line $n: bad amount — skipped"; continue; }
    memo=$(text_rtrim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$D_MEMO")")
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$date" "$((10#$seq))" "$code" \
      "$(charset_to_utf8 "$name")" "$amount" "$(charset_to_utf8 "$memo")"
  done < "$file"
)

# feed_header FILE — prints "date<TAB>source" from the H record.
feed_header() (
  export LC_ALL=C
  local line
  IFS= read -r line < "$1" || exit 1
  line=$(charset_strip_cr "$line")
  [ "$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_TYPE")" = H ] || exit 1
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_DATE")" \
    "$(text_rtrim "$(layout_slice "$line" "$H_SOURCE")")"
)

# feed_trailer FILE — prints "count<TAB>total" from the T record.
feed_trailer() (
  export LC_ALL=C
  local line last=""
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    line=$(charset_strip_cr "$line")
    [ "$(layout_slice "$line" "$REC_TYPE")" = T ] && last=$line
  done < "$1"
  [ -n "$last" ] || exit 1
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$((10#$(layout_slice "$last" "$T_COUNT")))" \
    "$((10#$(layout_slice "$last" "$T_TOTAL")))"
)

# ledger.sh — aggregation and control totals.

# ledger_totals NORMALIZED_TSV — per partner "code<TAB>count<TAB>sum<TAB>feedname",
# sorted by code. The feed name of the first record is kept for partners
# missing from the master.
ledger_totals() {
  awk -F '\t' '
    { c[$3]++; s[$3] += $5; if (!($3 in nm)) nm[$3] = $4 }
    END { for (k in c) printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\n", k, c[k], s[k], nm[k] }
  ' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k1,1
}

# ledger_sum NORMALIZED_TSV — "count<TAB>total" over all records.
ledger_sum() {
  awk -F '\t' '{ n++; t += $5 } END { printf "%d\t%d\n", n, t }' "$1"
}

# ledger_check FEED NORMALIZED_TSV — compares the trailer with what we read.
ledger_check() {
  local want got
  want=$(feed_trailer "$1") || { warn "no trailer in $1"; return 2; }
  got=$(ledger_sum "$2")
  if [ "$want" != "$got" ]; then
    warn "control totals differ: trailer=${want//$'\t'/ / } read=${got//$'\t'/ / }"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# money.sh — amounts in the feed are zero-padded whole won, 12 digits,
# with a trailing "-" in place of the last pad digit for refunds
# (e.g. "00000035000-" is -35000 on the older ERP build).

money_parse() {
  local s=$1 neg=0
  s=${s// /}
  if [ "${s: -1}" = "-" ]; then neg=1; s=${s%-}; fi
  case "$s" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  s=$((10#$s))
  if [ "$neg" -eq 1 ]; then s=$(( -s )); fi
  printf '%d' "$s"
}

# money_fmt 1250000 -> 1,250,000
money_fmt() {
  local n=$1 sign="" out=""
  if [ "${n:0:1}" = "-" ]; then sign="-"; n=${n#-}; fi
  while [ ${#n} -gt 3 ]; do
    out=",${n: -3}$out"
    n=${n:0:${#n}-3}
  done
  printf '%s%s%s' "$sign" "$n" "$out"
}

# partners.sh — partner master lookups.
#
# The master is exported by the same ERP as the feed, pipe-delimited:
#   CODE|NAME|REGION|STATUS        (STATUS: A active, I inactive)
# Names are loaded once per run into the "partners" cache.

partners_load() {

  require_file "$MASTER_FILE" "partner master"

    return 0

  cache_init partner_status

    code=$(text_trim "$code")

    name=$(charset_strip_cr "$name")
    status=$(charset_strip_cr "$status")
    cache_put partners "$code" "$(charset_to_utf8 "$name")"
    cache_put partner_status "$code" "${status:-A}"
    n=$((n + 1))
  done < "$MASTER_FILE"
  cache_stamp partners "$MASTER_FILE"
  log "partner master: $n entries"
}

  local v
  if v=$(cache_get partners "$1") && [ -n "$v" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$v"
  elif [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$2"
  else
    printf '(unknown %s)' "$1"
  fi
}

  local s
  s=$(cache_get partner_status "$1") || return 0

# text.sh — trimming and column layout for the text report.
# Hangul and other non-ASCII characters take two terminal columns.

text_rtrim() {
  local s=$1
  printf '%s' "${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
}

text_ltrim() {
  local s=$1
  printf '%s' "${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
}

text_trim() { text_ltrim "$(text_rtrim "$1")"; }

# Number of terminal columns TEXT occupies.
text_width() {
  local s=$1 ascii
  ascii=${s//[^[:ascii:]]/}
  printf '%d' $(( ${#ascii} + 2 * (${#s} - ${#ascii}) ))
}

# text_fit TEXT COLS — cut TEXT so that it fits in COLS columns, marking
# the cut with "~".
text_fit() {
  local s=$1 cols=$2 out="" ch w=0 cw i
  if [ "$(text_width "$s")" -le "$cols" ]; then printf '%s' "$s"; return; fi
  for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
    ch=${s:i:1}
    if [[ $ch == [[:ascii:]] ]]; then cw=1; else cw=2; fi
    (( w + cw > cols - 1 )) && break
    out+=$ch; w=$(( w + cw ))
  done
  printf '%s~' "$out"
}

# text_pad TEXT COLS — left-aligned, padded with spaces to COLS columns.
text_pad() {
  local s w
  s=$(text_fit "$1" "$2")
  w=$(text_width "$s")
  printf '%s%*s' "$s" $(( $2 - w )) ''
}

# text_lpad TEXT COLS — right-aligned.
text_lpad() {
  local w
  w=$(text_width "$1")
  printf '%*s%s' $(( $2 > w ? $2 - w : 0 )) '' "$1"
}

# Test helpers. Each test file sources this, calls t_setup, then asserts.
T_HOME=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
T_FAIL=0
T_PASS=0

t_setup() {
  T_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 't_cleanup' EXIT
  export SETTLE_WORK_DIR="$T_WORK/work"
  export SETTLE_OUT_DIR="$T_WORK/out"
  export SETTLE_FEED_DIR="$T_HOME/fixtures"
  export SETTLE_MASTER_FILE="$T_HOME/fixtures/partners.dat"
}

t_cleanup() { [ -n "${T_WORK:-}" ] && rm -rf "$T_WORK"; }

# Loads the libraries into the test shell (for unit tests).
t_source_libs() {
  export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
  export SETTLE_HOME="$T_HOME"
  . "$T_HOME/steps/_env.sh"
}

settle() { "$T_HOME/bin/settle" "$@"; }

ok()   { T_PASS=$((T_PASS + 1)); printf 'ok   - %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { T_FAIL=$((T_FAIL + 1)); printf 'FAIL - %s\n' "$1"; [ -n "${2:-}" ] && printf '       %s\n' "$2"; return 0; }

assert_eq() {
  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then ok "$1"; else fail "$1" "expected [$3] got [$2]"; fi
}

assert_contains() {
  if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qF -- "$3"; then ok "$1"; else fail "$1" "missing [$3]"; fi
}

assert_rc() {
  if [ "$2" -eq "$3" ]; then ok "$1"; else fail "$1" "expected exit $3 got $2"; fi
}

t_done() {
  printf '# %s: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$T_PASS" "$T_FAIL"
  [ "$T_FAIL" -eq 0 ]
}
